doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Did arrangers compare notes? Fletcher and Horace Henderson as writers
summary: Carter recalls no exchange with Redman or others, and says Fletcher's arranging was brought out later by Benny Goodman.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, we sort of touched on this question, but I’d just like to repeat it. As a player, obviously people would compare notes and, you know, musicians would compare what they’re doing and show each other things and help each other. Was there anything going on like that with people involved in this growing arranging as arrangements became more and more necessary as larger orchestras came into being and the stock arrangements would no longer suffice? Was there any interaction among arrangers as far as comparing notes and how you handle particular situations, or were people working pretty much on their own?
Gee, I don’t know. I can’t remember much of that. I don’t know. Do you have any names you might suggest of the period?

Well, for example, you and Don Redmond seemed to be locked in sort of a progressive . . . you know, you were following him sort of from various . . . in and out of various bands and things. Did you ever remember sitting down with Don Redmond and discussing anything?
Discussing anything? No. No, I don’t.
How about Fletcher’s own arranging? Now, when you were with the orchestra, was he doing any writing?
I didn’t know him as an arranger when I was in the orchestra. I think that’s something Benny Goodman brought out in him, you know.
Right. Do you recall any work that Horace Henderson, his work as an arranger or any of his writing?

Yeah, some of the things that he did was very interesting, and they sound even good today. Of course, so does Fletcher’s, you know. Big John Special, that was Horace’s. Oh, boy, there were some other things, but I can’t remember the titles.
Was he known to be writing much for Fletcher’s band while you were in it? I mean, were there a lot of Horace Henderson charts in the books?
I don’t think so, but there may have been, you know.
So when you joined, what was the book like? Was it things that Don Redmond had done before he left, primarily?
Yeah, mostly, for the most part, and there were things, as I said, that other arrangers had done, too, you know.
